key_insight: RNC-LM upgrades Levenberg-Marquardt with higher-order geometric corrections in Riemann normal coordinates so finite optimization steps stay more consistent with the model geometry.
engineering_relevance: This matters for scientific machine learning because it can make nonlinear least-squares training more robust in curved or ill-conditioned problems such as PINNs and large-scale surrogate fitting.
method: Reformulates the geodesic equation in a Riemann-normal-coordinate frame.
Adds arbitrary-order corrections beyond standard geodesic acceleration.
Uses a line search along the RNC curve to control step length while preserving LM-like cost reduction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved convergence on classical nonlinear least-squares benchmarks, relative L2 error near 1e-3 on a reaction-diffusion PINN failure case, and a 34-fold speedup on a large potential-energy-surface fitting task.
watch_item: Higher-order geometric updates add implementation and computation complexity, so performance may depend on accurate curvature information and careful step-control tuning.
paper_title: Higher-Order Geometric Updates for Levenberg-Marquardt Method via Riemann Normal Coordinates
